guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Acute Coronary Syndromes 2021
title: Angina episode at a football match
setting: Football stands. 60M spectator has mild chest discomfort, lightheaded, known history of angina. Carries GTN spray.
verdictExplanation: Chest pain with radiation to the arm, shortness of breath, and risk of myocardial infarction in a patient with active angina. Sick: administer GTN and monitor closely.

shared.danger: Stairs and crowds in football stands
shared.circulation: Fast pulse, skin is pale, cold, and clammy

history.history: Felt okay when arrived, developed chest discomfort radiating to left arm in the last 30 minutes

followUp.question: What is the priority first aid intervention for this patient?

options.text: Sit him in the 'W' position, administer 1-2 sprays of his GTN spray under the tongue, and call 999 if pain persists after 5 minutes
Help him stand up and walk down the stairs to the treatment room
Give him a cold cup of water and tell him to lie flat on the floor
Force him to walk around the concourse to relieve the indigestion

followUp.explanation: Sit the patient comfortably in the 'W' position. Administer 1-2 sprays of GTN under the tongue. If the pain does not ease after 5 minutes, give a second dose. If pain persists after 10 minutes or is severe/suspected heart attack, call 999 immediately. Never allow the patient to walk or stand.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Place in W-position, assist with GTN spray. Call 999 if pain is severe or does not resolve with GTN.
levelFlags.erNotes: ACS protocol. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%, give aspirin 300mg chewable if not already taken. Monitor BP and prepare AED in case of arrest.
